solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stuffed vine leaves and cheese back in sold out

indicators.note: going back means the cheese is read from its last letter to its first
sold out suggests letters knocked out of order, so the word sold is rearranged
in tells us the cheese sits inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A deli has run out of its stuffed vine leaves and its cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed cheese goes between the third and fourth letters of the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolmades are a Greek dish of vine leaves wrapped round a filling of rice or meat.

clue.text: Indian grass showing up a redness

indicators.note: in a down clue, showing up means the letters climb, so they are read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
rud is an old and dialect word for redness or ruddiness

explanation.surface: A grass in India is noticeable for its reddish colour.
explanation.walkthrough: RUD, as in ruddy, is a Chambers word for redness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dura, also spelt durra, is a grain sorghum grown in India and Africa.

clue.text: Sadly no acreage accepted for type of evening primroses

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters that follow are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
A is a commercial abbreviation for accepted, as written on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: A gardener sadly accepts that there is no land for growing evening primroses.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagraceae is the botanical family to which evening primroses and fuchsias belong.

clue.text: Count on American from the south getting stick

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means starting at the bottom and going upwards

blocks.note: to tell is to count, as in telling votes
AM is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone relies on an American from the southern states who is getting beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' reads like 'rely on', but count is one piece and on just places the next piece after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mallet is a hammer-like stick, as used in croquet or polo.

clue.text: Greek daughter in song finished loveless

indicators.note: loveless means without love, the zero score in tennis, so that round letter is dropped

blocks.note: an aria is a song in an opera
done means finished

explanation.surface: A Greek girl sings a song about a romance that has ended without love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, nil in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne was the daughter of King Minos of Crete in Greek myth, who helped Theseus out of the labyrinth.

clue.text: End with academic course in French town

blocks.note: to die is to end
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a degree course at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone finishes an academic course in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a Channel port in Normandy, northern France.

clue.text: Credit filling hospital food

indicators.note: filling means going inside something, so the credit abbreviation is put inside the hospital word

blocks.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A complaint that hospital food has been bought on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: Scran is British slang, originally naval and northern, for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Scran is an informal word for food or grub.

clue.text: Hard disk unwanted ?— it's fallen out of use

indicators.note: what is unwanted gets thrown away, so the disk-shaped letter is removed

blocks.note: solid means hard
O is round like a disk
surface padding: it completes the picture of obsolete hardware and adds no letters

explanation.surface: A computer's hard disk is no longer wanted because it is obsolete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of use' only finishes the surface story of discarded hardware; the definition is the single word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slid is a past participle of slide, and something that has slid has slipped or dropped down.

clue.text: Gap got rid of stores back in September

indicators.note: something that stores keeps another thing inside it
the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: to shed is to get rid of
the month's final letter

explanation.surface: A shop cleared away the gap in its stores back in September.
explanation.walkthrough: The month's last letter goes inside the word for got rid of, before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherd, a variant of shard, is a dialect word for a gap in a hedge.

clue.text: Old kilted plates a hit with the lads

blocks.note: to lam is to hit or thrash
lads are boys

explanation.surface: Old Scottish dishes were a big success with the young men.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamboys were the skirt-like hooped steel plates of a suit of armour, so 'kilted' describes them, not Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamboys is a historical armour term for the overlapping steel skirt worn below a breastplate.

clue.text: Loss of French corps in action

indicators.note: in places the military unit inside the word for action

blocks.note: de is French for of
an action is a lawsuit, a legal case
RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps

explanation.surface: French army corps suffer casualties in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' looks like combat but means a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrease is a reduction or diminution, a loss in size or number.

clue.text: Capital risk, second hundred goes missing in Scottish district

indicators.note: something that goes missing is no longer there, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: Paris is the French capital
a chance is a risk
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred; the second one in the risk word goes

explanation.surface: A capital-city gamble loses a second hundred pounds in a Scottish area.
explanation.walkthrough: The risk word has two Cs; 'second' says which one drops out.
explanation.definitionFit: Parischane is an old Scots word for a parish, a local church district.

clue.text: Gathered little resistance shown by United

indicators.note: little asks for a shortened form, here just the opening letter

blocks.note: R is also the physics symbol for resistance
allied means united

explanation.surface: A crowd assembled, but United's players put up little resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' suggests a football team but is simply a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to come together, so rallied means gathered or regrouped.

clue.text: The new primer is about pesticide

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around, so the fodder is put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new primer for painting contains a pest-killing chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Permethrin is a synthetic insecticide used against lice, ticks and mosquitoes.

clue.text: Article on monster Indian tree

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
the Gila monster is a venomous lizard of the American south-west

explanation.surface: A newspaper article reports a monster lurking in an Indian tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Agila is the eaglewood or aloes-wood tree of India, prized for its fragrant resin.

clue.text: Teacher associated with learner's close shave

indicators.note: a close is an ending, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a barbe was a Waldensian preacher or teacher
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A teacher has a close shave involving a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close shave' reads as a near miss, but close is the letter signal and shave alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To barber someone is to cut their hair or shave them, as a barber does.

clue.text: Veteran's gone astray in southern seaside town, as reported

definitions.note: 'Veteran's' marks the old usage of the past form

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

blocks.note: Ryde is a resort on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast

explanation.surface: An old soldier has wandered off somewhere in a south-coast resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Wry is an old verb meaning to swerve or go astray; 'Veteran's' says this is the archaic use.
explanation.definitionFit: Wried is the archaic past tense of wry, to turn aside or deviate from a course.

clue.text: What's great with riding for pleasure?

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
hacking is riding a horse at an ordinary pace for recreation

explanation.surface: A question about what makes leisure riding so wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Hacking is British for leisurely horse riding, as opposed to racing or competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacking is an informal intensifier meaning very large, as in a whacking great bill.

clue.text: Criticise what's put before me: famous oysters

blocks.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
in the sol-fa scale do and re come before me

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the oysters placed in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the third note of do-re-me, so the two notes before it follow the criticism word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandores were a celebrated kind of large oyster from the shores near Prestonpans in Scotland.

clue.text: Minutes are not including name for body of vassals

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so the name letter goes inside the contraction

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for minutes
the contraction aren't, apostrophe dropped
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Minutes of a meeting omit a name from a list of feudal tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: The name letter goes after the first letter of the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Manrent was a Scots feudal bond by which men pledged service to a lord, hence his body of vassals.

clue.text: Your chaps came out in a skin condition

indicators.note: came out suggests the letters have come out of their order and are rearranged
chaps are jaws, which close around whatever they hold

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Your men broke out in a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaps' reads as men, but chaps are jaws, which hold the old word for your inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecthyma is a skin infection producing large pus-filled sores, a deeper form of impetigo.

clue.text: Aberdonian shrink following origins of tiredness advised drug?

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so only the opening letters of the next two words are used

blocks.note: the first letter of each word
crine is a Scots verb meaning to shrink or shrivel; an Aberdonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scottish psychiatrist, noticing signs of tiredness, recommended medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a psychiatrist but is the Scots verb; the question mark marks the definition as a hint, since tacrine treats Alzheimer's rather than tiredness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacrine is a medicine once used to treat the memory loss of Alzheimer's disease.

clue.text: One about to get help at sea for swimmer

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so those letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a means one
ca is short for circa, about
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer in difficulty at sea is about to receive help.
explanation.definitionFit: An acaleph is a jellyfish or similar sea creature, which swims by pulsing its bell.

clue.text: More aware of the latest record in hot period

indicators.note: in puts the record inside the temperature abbreviation

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
an EP is an extended-play record
per is an abbreviation for period

explanation.surface: Someone is better informed about the newest record during a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-letter word around a two-letter one looks like a plain join; here the record simply follows the hot letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hep, older form of hip, means fashionably in the know, so hepper is the comparative: better informed on trends.

clue.text: Scholar's call for truce as if in for trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil calls for a truce as if heading for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A scholar here is a schoolchild: fains I, or fainites, is a British playground cry to call a pause in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Fains I is a schoolchildren's word claiming exemption or calling a truce during a game.

clue.text: One square metre area adopted by resort

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the area abbreviation goes inside the resort word

blocks.note: a resort is a holiday centre
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A one-metre-square plot has been taken over by a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A centare, or centiare, is a metric unit of land equal to one hundredth of an are, one square metre.

clue.text: High cost includes first-class fare from Mexico

indicators.note: includes means taking in, so the first-class letter joins the price word
high can mean drunk or intoxicated, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
A, as in A1, means first-class

explanation.surface: Expensive Mexican food comes with a first-class price tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacos are folded tortillas with a filling, a staple Mexican food.

clue.text: Look north and south for clubs in Scotland

blocks.note: an air is a look or appearance
N is the abbreviation for north
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Search everywhere for golf clubs in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Airn is Scots for iron, so airns are golf irons.
explanation.definitionFit: Airns is the Scots form of irons, the golf clubs with metal heads.

clue.text: About the start of restaurant meal, one's given out?

definitions.text: About the start of restaurant meal, one's given out?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
given out means sent away, so the letter for one leaves the meal word

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, about
the opening letter
tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: What gets handed out around the start of a restaurant meal?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a menu is given out at about the start of a restaurant meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A carte is a restaurant menu, as in à la carte, handed to diners when they sit down.

clue.text: One tailless rodent in container for deadly snake

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter is cut off
in puts the pieces inside the word for container

blocks.note: a kit is a tub or container
a means one
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rodent missing its tail is kept in a box for a poisonous snake to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit is an old word for a wooden tub or pail.
explanation.definitionFit: The karait, or krait, is a highly venomous snake of South Asia.

clue.text: Bass missing in clear sound

indicators.note: missing means absent, so the bass letter is taken away

blocks.note: bright means clear, as of a sky
B is the musical abbreviation for bass

explanation.surface: Music without a bass line comes through as a clear sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise but means correct or valid, as in a sound argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and sound both mean correct or justified, as in a right or sound judgement.

clue.text: Not entirely empty kennel for a dog

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A kennel stands not quite empty, waiting for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyke is a dog, especially a mongrel or cur; it also means a mischievous child.

clue.text: Forget about any drips with this whirling

definitions.text: Forget about any drips with this whirling

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out
whirling spins things round, so the remaining letters are churned into a new order

blocks.note: a is an abbreviation for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: With this machine whirling your washing, you need not worry about drips.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a spinning drum removes water so the clothes stop dripping.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin-dry is to remove water from washing by spinning it fast in a rotating drum.

clue.text: Nothing's in front of Nigel Havers that's simple and straightforward

indicators.note: the front of a name is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
nothing is zero, the letter O; ''s in' adds it next to the initial
havers is Scots for nonsense or foolish talk

explanation.surface: Nobody outshines the actor Nigel Havers, who is uncomplicated and direct.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Havers is an English actor; his surname is also Scots for nonsense. The O for nothing comes in after Nigel's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: No-nonsense means plain, practical and direct, free of frills or fuss.

clue.text: Pieces of grievous anarchy Trump supported?

indicators.note: in an across clue the leading letters of these words prop up the answer, read one after another from the front

blocks.note: the opening letter of each word
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political jibe that Trump backed grievous anarchy by way of guns.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces is gangster slang for guns, and so is gats.
explanation.definitionFit: Gats and pieces are both slang for pistols or handguns.

clue.text: Boiled Italian greens could make you retch as before

indicators.note: boiling churns things up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: It is the abbreviation for Italian
taken as written

explanation.surface: Overcooked Italian vegetables could turn your stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an old word: streigne is Spenser's spelling of strain, to retch or heave.
explanation.definitionFit: Streigne is an obsolete spelling of strain, to make an effort such as heaving or retching.
